name: Dynasort
summary: Shopify app that re-sorts collections, variant lists, search results and upsell blocks automatically, using recipes built from 60+ signals such as sales, margin, inventory and reviews.
best_for: Shopify stores with large or fast-changing catalogues where product order is a merchandising decision (seasonal ranges, frequent stock-outs, wide margin spreads) and nobody who wants to re-order collections by hand every week.
skip_if: your catalogue is small enough for one person to curate in an afternoon, the order barely changes, or you are not on Shopify: at $99 a month for the first paid tier, the sorting has to be earning its fee
honest_knock: Sorting driven by 40+ blended signals is powerful and opaque in the same breath: a recipe that ranks by margin, velocity and stock at once will sometimes bury a product you wanted seen, and there is real trial and error in getting the recipes to match how you actually merchandise. The jump from free to paid is steep at $99 a month, and it buys capacity rather than capability: search, recommendations and post-purchase are already in the free Demo, and Basic multiplies collections, recipes and serves (100,000 a month against 10,000). Above that the cards were printed under each other's headings in September and early October 2026; they read correctly on 17 November 2026, and A/B testing and the connector API sit on the free Demo card. And the evidence base is thin: 14 reviews, with thirteen fives and a single one-star and nothing in between. It is Shopify-only, so it is not an option if any part of your catalogue lives elsewhere.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/dynasort and in our own test the same day; earlier reads 14 and 15 September and 3 October 2026) Four tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Demo is free for as long as you like: 2 sorted and 2 managed collections, 10 recipes built from 40+ signals, a sort refresh every 60 minutes, variant sorting on 2 products, 10,000 recommendation serves a month, A/B testing and collection analytics, and a connector API for your stack or an LLM. Basic is $99 a month and adds, on top of Demo, 25 sorted and 10 managed collections, 20 recipes, a refresh every 30 minutes, variant sorting on 50 products, 100,000 serves a month and Customers Also Bought recipes. Pro is $249 a month for 100 sorted and 25 managed collections, 50 recipes, a refresh every 20 minutes, variant sorting on 200 products, 1 million serves a month, mobile versus desktop analytics, 30 day serving analytics and A/B tests of recommendation recipes. Enterprise is $499 a month for 1,000 sorted and 100 managed collections, 250 recipes, a refresh every 10 minutes, variant sorting on 5,000 products, unlimited serves, 365 day analytics with custom ranges and priority support and onboarding. Every paid tier carries a 30 day free trial. The mix up we recorded on 14 September and again on 3 October 2026, with the Pro and Enterprise capacity blocks under each other's headings, is gone: on 17 November 2026 the Pro card listed the 100 collection allowance and the Enterprise card the 1,000 collection allowance. The prices have not moved. In our own test on a Shopify development store the app showed a banner, “Special pricing for your store”, with Basic, Pro and Enterprise marked down by half ($99 to $49, $249 to $124 and $499 to $249) and an end date six days away; that is a temporary offer on the app's screen and not on the listing, so we do not count it as the price. The app's own text said any plan is free for 30 days, “You pay $0 today”, with a first charge on 17 December 2026. We chose Demo and saw no payment screen. The listing's rating block read 4.6 from 14 reviews, thirteen five star and one one star.
